answer: Sybil resistance is priced, not promised. Each agent identity must answer an epoch-randomized challenge from chain randomness, so replies cannot be precomputed or reused: duplicates are rejected before they attest. Every identity holds its own key and balance, an isolated island. Pretenders may wander across thousands of throwaway keys, but marginal cost never falls. The floor stays ferrous: real silicon, power, and fees. Bills grow linearly per fake identity, failed verification earns zero weight, so manufactured consensus pays what honest mining pays; takeover stays irrational.
